bib.title: Stellar Colosseum: A Many-Agent Harness for Long-Horizon Research in Mathematics and Theoretical Computer Science

legacy_report:
SOURCE: "Stellar Colosseum: A Many-Agent Harness for Long-Horizon Research in Mathematics and Theoretical Computer Science", Honghao Lin*, David P. Woodruff* (co-first), Yuan Deng, Jieming Mao, Song Zuo, Vahab Mirrokni. Google Research (Woodruff also Carnegie Mellon). arXiv 2609.15983v2 [cs.AI], 15 Sep 2026, preprint. Paper says the workflow is integrated into Google Antigravity "Teamwork" as the "Long Proof" pattern.

COVERAGE: Full read of the extraction, 76,736 chars, 27 pages, including both appendix pages of prompts (Appendix A.1 to A.4, to the revision instructions). References skimmed. No extraction faults. One quirk: the extraction runs words together ("introduceStellar"). No embedded instructions.

CORE CLAIM: A fixed-topology multi-agent pipeline (strategy exploration, readiness gate, DAG decomposition, parallel section solving, global verification, with revise or re-explore loops) is combined with a per-stage "candidates -> adversarial falsifier -> overlapping random-sample tree aggregation" pattern. Critiques stay attached to proposals, so objections survive synthesis. The authors say this is useful for research-level proofs and also transfers to competitive programming.

HEADLINE NUMBERS (all Gemini 3.1 Pro or 3.7 Flash, no cost or token figures given anywhere):
- TCS-Bench (n=300 theorem-proving tasks from FOCS/STOC/SODA 2020-2026), graded by a reference-assisted LLM grader. One Colosseum run per model, one candidate proof per problem. Direct Gemini 3.1 Pro 30.3%; Gemini 3.1 DeepThink 52.0%; GPT-5.6 Pro (max) 68.0%; Colosseum+3.1 Pro 54.0%; Colosseum+3.7 Flash 55.0%; cross-model selection 71.0% (213 problems, +48 over the better single run); oracle best-of-two 77.3%.
- The selection rule: 3.7 Flash writes 8 critiques of the 3.1 Pro proof. If at least 5 call it correct, submit it; otherwise submit the Flash proof. Critique-signal AUC is 0.896. Routing on 3.1 Pro's internal verifier alone gives 64.7%.
- Codeforces: 222 problems, clist difficulty above 1500, 52 contests (April to October 2025), hidden tests, all must pass. With a C++ execution probe: 218/222, performance rating 4263. Without: 213/222, rating 3918. This is the only ablation. The rating is the authors' own Elo-style calibration, not an official rating.
- Tree configs: strategy exploration widths (32,16,8,5,1), k=5; all other stages (16,8,5,1), k=5. Expected reuse is about 2 to 3 (e.g. 128 to 64 nodes at k=5 gives 2.5). Open-problem runs used trees of just over 100 leaves for exploration.
- Open research: five results in companion papers (coresets, sparse least squares hardness, MIPS dimension lower bound, Hadamard quantization, prefix-matrix factorization). Knuth cycles: 46- and 75-page proof drafts. Unit-distance problem: a 22-page draft after 15 exploration rounds, run with internet off.

QUOTES
- p.1/7: "Agreement among candidates can still hide a shared error, so a flat vote over final answers offers limited guidance for proofs."
- p.7: "Intermediate aggregation is constructive rather than a vote or ranking: it may merge compatible components, retain competing branches, repair a localized flaw, or declare an unresolved conflict."
- p.8: "The retry is local to the affected subproblem: completed work elsewhere in the dependency graph is preserved."
- p.9: "It is not a majority vote: a concrete fatal defect is sufficient to reject the proof, and generic acceptance judgments do not resolve it."

LIMITS
- There is no ablation of the core components: readiness gate, tree aggregation, falsifiers, knowledge directory, decomposition. The only ablation is the execution probe (213 to 218 of 222, one run).
- No compute, token or cost accounting. The authors concede that "Compute-matched evaluation would be needed to distinguish improved allocation from simply using more inference."
- No variance or repeat runs. The TCS-Bench grader is an LLM grader (reported above 90% accuracy on 100 labeled proofs). The 71.0% selection uses a second model, so it is an ensemble, and it is still below GPT-5.6 Pro's 68.0% only by a small margin (71.0 vs 68.0). Colosseum alone (54-55%) sits near DeepThink (52.0%) and below GPT-5.6 Pro.
- The authors concede that cross-system comparisons for research results are confounded: "Differences in human involvement, disclosure, and evaluation make it difficult to isolate the contribution of any one workflow component."
- Falsification "does not establish correctness". The paper offers no formal verification.
- Future work, not shown: clustering strategies, local restructuring after repeated subproblem failure, adaptive inference allocation, training on trajectories.
- No failure-mode study of multi-agent systems, no asynchronous agents, no context-window measurements. Roles and context isolation are described only through prompt templates.

BUILDS ON: Woodruff et al. 2026 (arXiv 2602.03837, Gemini case studies, parallel exploration and iterative verification); self-consistency (Wang et al., ICLR 2023); Tree of Thoughts (Yao et al., NeurIPS 2023); Self-Refine (Madaan et al., NeurIPS 2023); multiagent debate (Du et al., ICML 2024); Wu et al. ICLR 2025 (inference scaling, REBASE); Momus / "cognitive wells" (Dang et al. 2026); Aletheia (Feng et al. 2026); QED, ProofCouncil, RMA, Danus (role-separated verifier systems); LeanMarathon (DAG plus local repair); AlphaCode (Science 2022) and AlphaCode 2.

PLACEMENT: 07-orchestration is the best fit, but only partly. It fits role separation (explorer, falser, aggregator, gate, decomposer, solver, verifier), a topology (DAG with parallel eligible nodes, tree reduction), handoffs through typed schemas and a knowledge directory, and local retry. It is weak on subagents as context firewall, asynchronous agents, and when not to go multi-agent. 05-verification-loops fits second: the adversarial falsifier, the "no majority vote, one fatal defect rejects" rule, and the execution probe. 08 is not a fit. Treat it as a moderate, vendor-authored illustrative case, not strong evidence. The only controlled comparison is the execution-probe ablation.

FIGURE CANDIDATE: Figure 1 (p.2), "Overview of the Colosseum architecture": panel (a) is the stage pipeline with return edges (revise, re-explore, local retry); panel (b) is the overlapping sampling tree with a falsifier at each node. It shows the topology faster than prose.
